questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to a Parabola
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069054/assets/e0d18f7db92cfbe372f998e69d2395f2d586eb36cd25773588149c4ccf678eba.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the right-opening parabola shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola has its vertex at $O,$ and passes through the point $(3,6).$

The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(3,6)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=3$ and $y=6$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(6)^{2} & =4p(3) \\ 36 & =12p \\ p & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=12x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(12x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =12 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{6}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the left-opening parabola shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola has its vertex at $O,$ and passes through the point $(-8,4).$

The general equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=-8$ and $y=4$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(4)^{2} & =4p(-8) \\ 16 & =-32p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=-2x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-2x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-2 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Slope of the Tangent to an Ellipse
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069054/assets/ebef81911a434828ab94e643007d06b677538cdf0995198c7a065e35a8f81996.png)

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the ellipse shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Since our ellipse is centered at $(-1,-1)$ and has semiaxes $2$ and $1,$ its equation is given by

$$
\frac{(x-(-1))^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-(-1))^{2}}{{1}^{2}}=1\,⟹\,\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}+(y+1)^{2}=1.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4}+(y+1)^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(x+1)^{2}}{4})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}((y+1)^{2}) & =0 \\ \frac{2(x+1)}{4}+2(y+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ 2(y+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x+1}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x+1}{4(y+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the ellipse shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
Since our ellipse is centered at $(0,1)$ and has semiaxes $2$ and $3,$ its equation is given by

$$
\frac{(x-0)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1\,⟹\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{9}=1.
$$

Now, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{9}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{4})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{9}) & =0 \\ \frac{2x}{4}+\frac{2(y-1)}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =0 \\ \frac{2(y-1)}{9}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{x}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{9x}{4(y-1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ for the right-opening parabola shown above. Express the answer in terms of the variable $y.$

$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola has its vertex at $O,$ and passes through the point $(6,-2).$

The standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0)$ is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Substituting $x=6$ and $y=-2$ into the equation above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2)^{2} & =4p(6) \\ 4 & =24p \\ p & =\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of our parabola is 

$$
{y}^{2}=\frac{2}{3}x.
$$

Finally, to calculate $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use implicit differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2}{3}x) \\ 2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{3y}\end{aligned}
$$
